name: Esker Foundation
watch: Founder wealth from oil and gas.
why_flagged: Founder wealth from oil and gas.
records_note: No annual reports, donor list or board found in archived pages of its site; its charity accounts could not be checked.

name: Fábrica de Arte Cubano
funding: Founded by musician X Alfonso. In 2014 the Cuban Music Institute and Ministry of Culture were covering some costs until it became self-financing.
watch: The ministry's music centre cancelled a Celia Cruz tribute there in October 2025. It closed temporarily in June 2026; Prensa Latina blames the US embargo.
why_flagged: Founded by musician X Alfonso. In 2014 the Cuban Music Institute and Ministry of Culture covered some costs until it became self-financing. It occupies a state-owned building.
records_note: Its site offers two dossiers and nothing else: no annual report, accounts, sponsor list or board.

name: Festival Internacional Cervantino
funding: 2023 budget 168.8M pesos: federal culture ministry 65.3M, Guanajuato 36M, guest country and state 42M, embassies 10.2M, sponsors 15.4M. Sponsors include Yamaha, Mazda, Megacable, HONOR and the FEMSA group.
watch: Name to know: Coca-Cola FEMSA, a named sponsor. Chiapas groups have sought to revoke its water permit since 2017; no campaign targets the festival.
why_flagged: Name to know: Coca-Cola FEMSA, a named sponsor. Chiapas groups have sought to revoke its water permit since 2017; no campaign targets the festival.
records_note: Names sponsors on a 2025 edition page and lists its government hosts and programming committee; no annual reports or audited accounts exist online.

name: Fire Station: Artist in Residence
watch: An excluded funder runs it now: Qatar Museums, a Gulf state body under labour critique, operates and funds it. The Peninsula (16 Nov 2025) reports QM running its residency shows.
why_flagged: An excluded funder runs it now: Qatar Museums, a Gulf state body under labour critique, operates and funds it. The Peninsula (16 Nov 2025) reports QM running its residency shows.
records_note: Part of Qatar Museums, which posts no annual reports, accounts or sponsor names; its board is named only in state press.

name: Fondation Cartier
funding: Created in 1984 by Cartier SA and funded by Cartier, part of Richemont. Moved to a new Jean Nouvel site at the Palais-Royal, reopening 25 October 2025.
watch: Its architecture commissions and programming are funded directly from the corporate balance sheet of jeweler Cartier / Richemont.
why_flagged: In 2023 Yanomami leaders and anthropologist Bruce Albert criticised Cartier's greenwashing use of a Yanomami photo. Cartier removed it and called it an oversight.
records_note: No annual report, accounts, funder list or board is posted; the site names its founder, a president and a managing director only.

name: Fondation Louis Vuitton
watch: The Cour des comptes (November 2018) said the donations could amount to sponsorship promoting LVMH. Anticor challenged the secrecy of its accounts.
why_flagged: The Cour des comptes (November 2018) said the donations could amount to sponsorship promoting LVMH. Anticor challenged the secrecy of its accounts.
records_note: No annual reports, accounts, donor list or board found; the Conseil d'Etat ruled in 2022 that its accounts cannot be released to third parties.

name: Fondazione Palazzo Strozzi
funding: 2025 income EUR 11.7M. Fondazione CR Firenze gave 1.1M, the Partners Committee 928k, the Recordati foundation 600k, Intesa Sanpaolo 464k. City, Region and Metropolitan City gave 500k each.
watch: Enegan, a Florence retailer of gas and power, is a Partner and has supplied the Fondazione's renewable electricity since 2021. Visitors in 2025: 384,176.
why_flagged: 2025 income EUR 11.7M. Fondazione CR Firenze gave 1.1M, the Partners Committee 928k, the Recordati foundation 600k, Intesa Sanpaolo 464k. City, Region and Metropolitan City gave 500k each.
records_note: Reports run from 2007 to 2025, accounts with a KPMG audit are posted, the 2025 report names funders with amounts, and the board is listed.

name: Fondazione Prada
funding: Chaired by Miuccia Prada. 2019 revenue was €25.2M from tickets, catalogues and sponsorship contracts; it received no donations that year.
watch: Private institution funded by the Italian luxury fashion house Prada. Its operations and capital investment depend on Prada's commercial revenues.
why_flagged: Prada withdrew its Pradamalia figurines in December 2018 after blackface criticism and boycott calls. No flagged funder and no protest at the foundation found.
records_note: Posts an institutional report covering 2017 to 2019 with summary financials and its board; it names no sponsors and reports no donations in 2018.

name: Fragmentos, Espacio de Arte y Memoria
funding: Colombian Ministry of Culture space run by the Museo Nacional.
watch: In May 2021 President Duque held a political meeting in the space; Francis Alÿs withdrew his show and Doris Salcedo protested.
why_flagged: Colombian Ministry of Culture space run by the Museo Nacional. Entry is free and no private sponsor is named.
records_note: The space's own site publishes no reports, accounts, sponsor list or board; it sits under the Ministry of Culture and Museo Nacional.

name: Fridericianum
watch: A 2025 Marisa Merz show was cancelled over the funders' post-documenta code of conduct.
why_flagged: A 2025 Marisa Merz show was cancelled over the funders' post-documenta code of conduct.
records_note: Fridericianum posts no reports or funder list and names only its supervisory board chair; its imprint names the city of Kassel and Hesse as owners.

name: Fringe World
watch: Ended Woodside in 2023 after a five-year campaign.
why_flagged: Ended Woodside in 2023 after a five-year campaign.
records_note: Artrage, Fringe World's organiser, posts its 2025-26 annual report, files accounts with the ACNC, shows 2026 partner logos, and lists its board.

name: Frist Art Museum
watch: Recurring nurses' union protests at the gala over HCA.
why_flagged: Recurring nurses' union protests at the gala over HCA.
records_note: It posts community reports (2005 and 2025 seen), audited statements for 2022 to 2024, partners as of September 2025, and trustees.
